nodes.text: Obtain IR spectra to identify functional groups
Obtain isomers from molecular formula C16H12O3
IR peak at 1732 cm-1 indicates carbonyl group; 3415 cm-1 suggests OH group; 3100-3050 cm-1 consistent with aromatic C-H

support.quote: The IR spectra show a peak at 1732 cm⁻¹, which is indicative of a carbonyl group (C=O). The peaks around 3415 cm⁻¹ suggest the presence of an -OH group, possibly indicating a carboxylic acid or an alcohol. The peaks in the range of 3100-3050 cm⁻¹ are consistent with aromatic C-H stretching

The carbon NMR spectra show multiple peaks, including those in the aromatic region (around 120-160 ppm) and some in the aliphatic region (around 14.26 ppm and 61.10 ppm). This suggests the presence of an aromatic ring and possibly an aliphatic chain or functional group.

The mass spectrometry spectra indicate a molecular ion peak at m/z 276.07, suggesting a molecular weight of approximately 276 g/mol. The presence of isotopic peaks suggests the presence of elements like chlorine or bromine

The IR spectra show a peak at 1732 cm⁻¹, which is indicative of a carbonyl group (C=O). The peaks around 3415 cm⁻¹ suggest the presence of an -OH group, possibly indicating a carboxylic acid or an alcohol. The peaks in the range of 3100-3050 cm⁻¹ are consistent with aromatic C-H stretching
